description: [S7.10] The app's sim context keeps the device-less sound path of the pinned corpus (g_soundReady 0, no initSound in the port's boot): its requests (playSound, startSoundSlot, Snd::status, loadSoundTable, arrayStaticInit_448160) are copied to the shadow audio context before they run (audio_exe Req depth 0) and the sim gets the device-less answers. Control flow the original takes on device answers follows the device-less original instead: Snd::status's value, Snd::play's and Snd::busy's timeGetTime reads (exe sites kSiteSndPlayClock / kSiteSndBusyClock in audio_exe.h) and the extra sound.dll clock read before seedFromTime that a device adds at boot (CLAUDE.md batch b2: seed_time 0x00100001 with a device, 0x00100000 without). The shadow's answers are discarded.
path to resolution: design decision of the S7 lead (GameState unchanged); a device-faithful sim would need traces recorded with a device and new references

description: [S7.10] sound.dll keeps its window as g_soundWindow (field +8 of SoundWindowObj, sound.dll rva 0xb49b8) only when SetWindowLongA(window, GWL_WNDPROC, soundWindowSubclassProc) returns non-zero (SoundWindowObj_subclass rva 0x286f0: `if (!r) return 0x18` at 0x28712, the store at 0x28721); S4's DeviceSink answers 0, so every completion message (0x7ee from postNotification, 0x7eb from the mixer) went to hwnd 0 and a slot never played twice. The app sink answers a previous-procedure token (1 << 12) outside Model mode and delivers each message posted to the window to soundWindowSubclassProc on the audio thread right after the call that posted it; the original's main thread dispatches it at its next message pump, so the delivery time differs. Messages to hwnd 0 are dropped (none in the title session once the window is kept).
path to resolution: measure on the original with a device: the thread and frame of each 0x7ee / 0x7eb dispatch (a Frida hook on soundWindowSubclassProc), compared with the shadow's delivery

description: [S7.10] The capture device's cursors: GetCurrentPosition answers the software play position and a write cursor 10 ms of frames ahead (ds_sink.cpp position()); DirectSound's real write-cursor lead is not measured. With it the engine starts a click 0.43-0.46 s after its playSound request (title session: request at 0.0 / 0.9 / 1.8 / 2.7 s, sound at 0.460 / 1.330 / 2.230 / 3.130 s), because it writes ahead in its 64 KB stream buffer (22050 Hz stereo 16-bit, 0.74 s); the latency on a real device follows the real cursors.
path to resolution: record GetCurrentPosition answers and the first non-silent Unlock offset on a device (DSound mode), and the original's own latency

description: [S7.10] The capture mix (ds_sink.cpp render()) is a model of DirectSound's software mixer: linear interpolation between neighbouring frames for a frequency change, gain 10^(volume / 2000), pan as the other side's attenuation 10^(-abs(pan) / 2000), 16-bit clip, a non-looping buffer stopped at its end with its position back at 0. The judge (test_app_audio.py) upsamples its 22050 Hz reference to the 44100 Hz primary format with the same linear interpolation, so that rule is shared by sink and judge, not judged. Pan and frequency are not judged at all on the title session: the engine sends no SetPan to a DS buffer and SetFrequency only with the buffers' own 22050 Hz (both controls equivalent, captures byte-identical).
path to resolution: a session that pans or pitches a static-buffer sound at the device, and a real-device recording (loopback capture) to compare the interpolation

description: [S7.10] Real-time cost of the shadow's timer tick (fire(), 3 runs each at 35 % machine load, LIVING-PC, MSVC Release): title session (1-2 voices) x64 0.10 ms mean / 0.68 ms max, Win32 0.25 / 1.12; the device run with 178 sounds started at once (13 voices) x64 16.5-17.2 ms mean / 24.3 max, Win32 32.3-36.9 ms mean / 122 max against the 30 ms period: Win32 does not keep up with that many voices (late ticks are skipped beyond four periods). Why Win32 (real x87) is about 2x slower than x64 (software 80-bit) is not measured.
path to resolution: profile the Win32 tick (dispatcher, x87 unit save / restore per call) and count voices in real sessions

description: [S7.10] The DSound backend (real dsound.dll buffers: CreateSoundBuffer, the Unlock copy, Play / Stop / SetVolume / SetFrequency, GetCurrentPosition / GetStatus from the real buffer) has not run against a device: on 2026-10-29 DirectSoundCreate returned DSERR_NODRIVER (0x88780078) on LIVING-PC (its only endpoint is the TV's HDMI one, off). With no device the shadow ran on the model's answers, silent, failed 0, the sim unchanged (S7.11's case).
path to resolution: run `simgolf_audio_check script --mode dsound` and `simgolf_port --audio on` with the TV on; Mariano listens (gate d)

description: [S7.10] Long sessions: the shadow uses S4's DeviceSink heap (16 MB chunks from 0xF4000000, at most 8, a freed block reused only by an allocation of its exact rounded size) and its model of mmio. A session that loads and frees many large static-buffer sounds (music, 1-6 MB each) can exhaust it; MissingResource stops the shadow (silence, first_error in audio.json), the sim continues. Not measured over a long session.
path to resolution: an app session of a game year with --audio capture, reading the arena use
